claims.statement: `Batch.documents` is produced by two independent data layers — `getBatchDocumentsSnapshot`/`mapDocumentRows` in `modules/documents/data/documents.ts` and `mapDocumentsMap` in `modules/batches/data/batches.ts` — which duplicate `mapDocumentRow`, the `MISSING_DOC` constant and the backfill loop, because `eslint.config.mjs` makes each module's `data/` private so the copies cannot be imported from each other and must be kept in sync by hand.

Both data layers backfill every key in the batch's own `program_document_requirements` catalog to a `MISSING_DOC` record before overlaying real rows, so 'no submitted row means missing' is decided in the data layer (ADR-004 D1) and a key still absent afterwards is one the batch's catalog never listed.

`program_document_requirements` rows are the per-program requirement catalog and its snapshot type deliberately has no `no-tenant-access` member: the catalog is reference data, so an empty result means unseeded rather than no access.

`document_key` is configured per-program data rather than a closed enum, so mapping and validation treat it by shape: `mapRequirementRow` falls back to a generic icon for an unknown key and `buildEvidencePath` validates the key's character shape instead of checking membership.

A requirement added after a batch started legitimately diverges from that batch's tracked keys, and the mock and DB catalogs were kept separate so the mismatch stays visible — the ADR's purpose is to make that divergence legible rather than fatal or dishonest.

Status is read only through `modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts`: `docRecordFor` returns `null` for an absent key, and there is deliberately no `'untracked'` member of `DocStatus` because the union mirrors the DB enum and is assigned straight off a row (ADR-004 D5).

Measurement and gating answer untracked requirements in opposite directions: `summarizeDocCompliance` excludes untracked keys from numerator and denominator while `isDocOnFile` returns false for them, so the same batch can read 100% on file and still be blocked — both directions fail safe, and a test pins the disagreement.

`summarizeDocCompliance` computes `onFilePct` and `verifiedPct` via a helper that returns `null` when the denominator is zero, so the KPI is `null` — never 0 or 100 — when nothing is tracked, forcing every consumer to render the unknown case.

`blockingDocumentNames` returns configured display labels rather than requirement keys because FR-06 AC-1 forbids showing a raw `document_key`, and `blockingDocuments` partitions criticals first instead of sorting so an empty catalog yields an empty summary rather than a blocked batch.

The matrix screen's column set is `requirementCatalogOf(batches)` — the union of every shown program's catalog, display only — while completeness is scored per batch against its own `criticalRequirements`; with no catalog at all the view renders one 'requirements unavailable' state instead of a grid of empty rows. The route derives those columns from the already tenant-access-folded batch snapshot, so a no-tenant-access read renders `NoTenantAccessState` before any grid exists.

`DocumentsView.docOf` narrows on the batch's own catalog before calling `docRecordFor`, so a leftover record outside that catalog still renders as 'Not tracked'; untracked cells are disabled, carry an explanatory title, and are skipped by the click handler.

Cell state ladder: `verified`/`submitted` open `FilePreviewModal`, `pending`/`missing` raise an attach toast for writers, untracked is inert; verification is an admin-only local override keyed `batchId:key` that is refused when the profile has no display name, and no write reaches the database from the screen.

Evidence object keys follow `{tenant_id}/{batch_id}/{document_key}/{filename}`, and that convention is the authorization check itself: the bucket's select, insert and update policies call `app_private.can_access_tenant((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)`, so a filename containing a separator shifts segments and relocates the object out of the caller's tenant folder.

`buildEvidencePath` validates in fixed order — tenant id, batch id, document key, filename — using anchored UUID regexes, a lowercase key shape, and a filename guard that rejects separators, control characters, bare `.`/`..`, percent-encoded separators, surrounding whitespace and over-length names; a test asserts the tenant is checked first so the reason is never misleading.

Path and file entry points return discriminated results rather than throwing so FR-06's invalid-type, upload-rejected and upload-failed states stay distinguishable, with `EVIDENCE_REJECTION_COPY` supplying per-reason copy that leaks no identifier, table or bucket name.

`validateEvidenceFile` enforces a 52 428 800-byte limit inclusively, rejects non-finite and non-positive sizes, normalizes MIME parameters and case, and checks size before type so an oversized file is not blamed on its format; the limit must stay equal to the bucket's `file_size_limit`.

The evidence bucket is private, so every read is a time-limited signed URL (300 s default) with no public-URL path; uploads pass `upsert: false` so re-submission creates a new object and leaves the prior one intact for auditors.

The canonical migration's evidence policies are select/insert/update only; `20260910120000` adds a DELETE policy gated on `can_manage_tenant`, deliberately tighter than the `can_access_tenant` used by the read and upload policies. `evidence.ts` still exposes no `deleteEvidence`.

`getSignedEvidenceUrl` re-validates the stored path by splitting it and rejoining trailing segments, so a key with extra segments fails `isSafeFilename` instead of validating a shorter path than the one actually signed — the column is unconstrained `text` and could be edited by hand.

The evidence code is ungated ahead of the UI: `buildEvidencePath`, `uploadEvidence` and `getSignedEvidenceUrl` have no callers, so `FilePreviewModal` treats any non-null `file.url` as a real file, invents a `name.pdf` and renders a simulated page, while `mapDocumentRow` sets `url` to the bare `storage_path` object key (or the external URL).

Evidence calls return `unconfigured` when Supabase is unset and an opaque `sync-failed` message when Storage errors, because raw Supabase/SQL errors are not rendered; an absent signed URL alongside a null error is also treated as failure rather than returning an empty link.

The evidence path must be derived from tenant/batch/document identity rather than accepted from the client: the browser contributes only the file name, ids are anchored UUID regexes because they are interpolated into the object key before Postgres casts them, and the `document_key` guard keeps the `documents_batch_id_document_key_key` upsert key unambiguous once a file name is appended.

The four document/evidence test files cover only the pure domain helpers, the duplicated mappers and the path builder; the Storage I/O half of `evidence.ts` is mocked or uncovered, so a green suite is not proof of the bucket round trip.
